mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined for two consecutive weeks (-23.7 to -27.1 to -28.3). Momentum in mobility indices tends to persist absent an external shock, so the downward trend in retail footfall will continue over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell from -23.7 at t-2w to -28.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days despite two prior weeks of consecutive decline, rejecting the momentum assumption.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility is oscillating near a low band (-38.1 to -31.6 to -34.3 to -33.0). If TRANSIT falls below -35 points again, this signals renewed restriction on movement that will suppress retail trips within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -35 points in any subsequent week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT ranged between -38.1 and -31.6 over the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat in the two weeks following a TRANSIT reading below -35, despite the threshold being crossed.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous softening in WORKPLACES (-34.7 to -28.0) and TRANSIT (-38.1 to -33.0) jointly reduce commute-linked incidental shopping trips. The combined weakening of both series, rather than either alone, drives a compounding reduction in retail footfall over two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain substantially below baseline across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next two weeks even though both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain depressed or decline further, indicating no compounding commute effect.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL time has steadily declined from 9.6 to 6.7 over four weeks, indicating households are spending progressively less time at home. This gradual normalization signals a reopening regime that will raise retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell monotonically from 9.6 at t-3w to 6.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL continuing its monotonic decline, invalidating the reopening-linkage mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility dropped sharply from 0.9 at t-2w to -12.6 at t-1w, likely reflecting a weather or seasonal shift reducing outdoor substitution for leisure. When PARKS falls more than 10 points week-on-week, displaced outdoor activity shifts toward indoor retail and recreation within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 0.9 at t-2w to -12.6 at t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week following a greater-than-10-point weekly drop in PARKS, indicating no substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has been improving steadily from -11.0 to -9.6, indicating rising willingness to make discretionary in-person errands. This recovery in essential-shopping confidence is a leading indicator that non-essential retail visits will also rise over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -11.0 at t-3w to -9.6 at t-0w with only a minor dip at t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline over the next 28 days even as GROCERY_PHARM keeps improving, breaking the assumed leading-indicator relationship.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous one-week drop in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT would indicate a fresh tightening of restrictions, since both series normally move together under policy shocks. Such a joint drop would suppress retail visits sharply within one week due to combined reduction in commuting and discretionary mobility.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both fall more than 5 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT show parallel declines between t-2w and t-1w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week following a joint drop of more than 5 points in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: In a steady-state regime with PARKS mobility recovering toward baseline (e.g., from -15.1 to -10.7 over four weeks) alongside declining RESIDENTIAL time, increased outdoor leisure activity competes with and diverts footfall from retail and recreation venues over a two-week window.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -15.1 at t-3w to -10.7 at t-0w while RESIDENTIAL fell from 9.6 to 6.7
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks concurrently with continued PARKS recovery and RESIDENTIAL decline, indicating no substitution away from retail toward outdoor activity.
